Subject: Renewal pricing request & mid-contract growth smoothing

Hi Olga,

Hope you’re well — we’re coming up on the renewal window and have a couple of moving pieces on our side. Q2 run-rate exceeded our committed capacity by ~28% due to a seasonal pilot (see attached usage summary). Procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a renewal path that:

- Smooths the mid-contract uplift so we don’t take a single-step price shock
- Protects our unit cost for sustained growth through the next 12 months
- Keeps co-term intact with our billing cycle (Nov 1) if possible

We’d love to see a concrete proposal that blends a transitory cushion with a usage-driven discount schedule — ideally something your team can sign off quickly so procurement can budget. Attaching the Q2 CSV for context.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Director of Platform Ops
HelixHealth

Attachment: Helix_Usage_Summary_Q2.csv (CSV, 54 KB)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing request & mid-contract growth smoothing

Hi Aisha — thanks for the usage file, that’s helpful.

Quick read: growth is concentrated in specific models and peak windows (clear seasonal bump). We can approach this three ways and combine them:

1) Short-term bridge credits to absorb the Q2 delta, phased over 3 months.
2) A graduated tier discount tied to 30/60/90 day sustained usage (keeps unit economics aligned).
3) Optional burst buffer capacity at a slightly higher rate for unpredictable spikes (pay-as-you-go).

I attached an initial bridge table (v1) and a sketch of discount bands. Marcus and Naomi — can you sanity-check band thresholds and the financial impact? If this looks reasonable, I’ll send Aisha a formal blended proposal with a DocuSign-ready statement.

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Proposed_Bridge_Table_v2.xlsx (Excel, 72 KB)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing request & mid-contract growth smoothing

Olga — notes on the banding after quick P&L:

- Recommend 10% bridge credit that covers the immediate Q2 overage, amortized over three billing cycles.
- Discount bands: 0-75% committed run-rate = list price; 75-110% = 7% unit discount; 110-160% = 12% unit discount; above 160% = burst buffer pricing.
- Add a seasonal buffer clause: one time per year Helix can trigger a 30-day temporary smoothing credit (requires 48-hour notice).

Tradeoffs: the buffer clause reduces churn risk but caps downside; we should gate the largest discount on a minimum 12-month renewal term.

Naomi: will this play cleanly with procurement? Tessa: any operational constraints on offering the 30-day trigger?

—Marcus

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@helixhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: HelixHealth renewal — blended bridge & usage-smoothing proposal

Hi Aisha — following up with a concrete proposal based on your Q2 file and our internal review. Summary (high level):

- Bridge credit: one-time 10% credit applied to Q2 overage, amortized across next three invoices (applies only to model categories A/B as listed in the attached table).
- Graduated unit discount: 75–110% run-rate => 7% discount; 110–160% => 12% discount (applies to base compute tokens only).
- Seasonal buffer: Helix may request a single 30-day smoothing credit per 12-month term; requires 48-hour notice and usage justification.
- Burst buffer: Pay-as-you-go capacity for peaks at a 20% premium to list (no commitment).
- Term & co-term: 12-month renewal, co-term Nov 1. Minimum commitment: maintain at least current committed capacity for the first 3 months post-renewal to qualify for the 12% band.

Next steps:
1) If this model sounds good, I can circulate a DocuSign statement with the bridge/discount schedule and the co-term date.
2) Procurement to confirm the preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) so we can finalize amortization.

I’ve attached the proposed bridge table and a ready-to-sign renewal statement. If you want to tighten the bands or prefer a different amortization window, we can adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly for budget planning.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed_Bridge_Table_v2.xlsx (Excel, 72 KB); DocuSign_Renewal_Stmt.pdf (PDF, 48 KB);

Olga — thanks, this is exactly the practical framing procurement wanted. Quick notes:

- Procurement prefers quarterly billing for amortization — ok to apply the 10% bridge credit across three quarters.
- The seasonal buffer clause sounds fair; please add a one-paragraph definition of acceptable justification for the request (e.g., pilot, known campaign, not retrospective anomaly).
- We’re good with the co-term Nov 1 and the 12-month renewal; will need to run legal on the minimum commitment clause but unlikely to block it.

Please send the DocuSign statement with the clarified seasonal buffer language and we’ll route to finance/legal. Appreciative of the fast turnaround.

Best,
Aisha
Director of Platform Ops, HelixHealth
